summary: Tarthang Tulku works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, having studied under traditional teachers including A-'gyur Rinpoche, Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima, and Jamyang Khyentse Chokyi Lodro (~1950–1959). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), Padma Ling (~1969), Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Tsering works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied under Burmiok Athing and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche. He held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (1980), Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), Northwest Minzu University (2000), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Bulletin of Tibetology.

Tatiana Oranskaia specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and under committee member Orna Almogi, and served as Prof. Dr. at the University of Hamburg (1995).
Tatsugen Sato was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held positions at Komazawa University (~1973–1995), Ryukoku University, and Tokai University.
Tatsuhiro Saito works in Buddhist studies, having studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He also founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.
Tatsuo Nishida worked in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1951), where he later served as a professor (~1971–1992).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Luang Por Teean Jittasubho (1980) and at the University of Hawaii (M.A. ~1988). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1981–1983), Mahidol University (~1994), and World Buddhist University (~2005).
Tej Ram Sharma works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University (~1964–1968) and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University in 1978.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1948–1953). He later held posts at Ryukoku University (~1974–1999), Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~1999–2004), Otani University, Kyoto Women's University, and Tenri University.
Tenshin Tanouye worked in Buddhist studies, studying under traditional teacher Sogen Omori (~1970–1994). He also founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied for a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo (~2006–2008) under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik.

Tenzin Dorjee works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under traditional teachers Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He served as General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery (-1999) and as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of British Columbia, and under traditional teachers Trijang Rinpoche (~-1981), Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (~1968–1977), Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1976–1991), and Trulshik Rinpoche (~1960–2011).

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (Geshe -1986) and under several traditional teachers. He held posts as president of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991), and at Ligmincha International (~1992).

Ter Ellingson works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College (1966), the University of Chicago (1970), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979), and served at the University of Washington (1981–2016).

Terese Tse Bartholomew worked in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. After completing an M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles (~-1965), she was Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (~1968–2007).
Terry Kleeman works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (~1978–1988) and served as a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1998–2021).

Teruji Ishizu was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held posts at Tohoku University (~1941–1967), Keio University (~1967–1972), the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, and Aichi University.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia, among others. She held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~1991–1993), and Florida State University (1993).
Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1931). He held positions at Ryukoku University (~1970–1982), Gifu Kyoritsu University, and Taisho University.
